finding_key: packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts::anyone can start a `mode=cli` login pointing at an arbitrary loopback port; the new browser-binding cookie does not stop the start-url variant of the phishing attack it is documented as closing
evidence: Verified against the supplied code: `GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate` (github-auth.guard.ts, the `mode === 'cli' && port` branch) accepts an unauthenticated start request with any `port` in 1024–65535 plus attacker-chosen `nonce` and `code_challenge`, and mints the `wafflebase_oauth_state` cookie *on the browser making that request*. So if the victim clicks an attacker-crafted start URL, the victim's own browser holds the binding, `verifyCallbackState` (auth.controller.ts, CLI branch: `state.mode === 'cli' && secretEquals(state.browserBinding, binding)`) passes, and the controller redirects to `http://127.0.0.1:<attacker-chosen port>/callback?code=<victim code>&state=<attacker nonce>`; because the attacker supplied the challenge they hold the verifier, so `consumeCode` in cli-auth.store.ts happily redeems it. The cookie therefore only defeats the pre-minted-state/replay variant, while the guard comment and the rest-api.md risk row assert it closes "an attacker mints a CLI state pointing at a loopback port they own and walks the victim through consent" — a scope overclaim, and PKCE gives no protection here either. Exploitation still requires the attacker to have a listener on the victim's loopback (shared/multi-user host or a local malicious process) plus a clicked link, which caps impact, but the outcome is full account takeover of the victim's tokens.
